Recent unreviewed agent-repo commits include new cron handler `agents/may/handlers/tool-quality-scan.ts` and multiple gym scenarios (per `git log`/`git show` in `/app/agents`).

## Findings

### IMPORTANT — `tool-quality-scan.ts` baseline/regression key fragmentation risk (tool name normalization)
- File: `agents/may/handlers/tool-quality-scan.ts`
- Evidence: category key is built as ``${chain.trigger?.tool || "unknown"}:${classifyFailure(chain)}`` (see `scanToolQuality()` loop), and baseline stores metrics under the same keys.
- Risk: if upstream evaluation data contains inconsistent tool labels (`Bash` vs `bash`, missing tool → `unknown`), baseline keys will fragment and regressions may be noisy or miss real changes.
- Recommendation: normalize tool name at key time, e.g. `(chain.trigger?.tool||'unknown').toLowerCase()`; consider whether tool should be part of regression key or tracked separately.

### IMPORTANT — optimizer task injection logs no underlying error
- File: `agents/may/handlers/tool-quality-scan.ts`
- Evidence: injection is wrapped in `try { ... } catch { ctx.log("[tool-quality-scan] ⚠️ Failed to inject optimizer task."); }` without logging the thrown error.
- Impact: reduces debuggability for an ops-critical cron.
- Recommendation: `catch (e) { ctx.log(String(e)); ... }` (or include stack if `e instanceof Error`).
